$comment: contract-version 0.7.0 — `digestProviders` is NOT native-only. ANY plugin may contribute an in-process digest provider and the workspace runtime loads it BY DEFAULT; `native` (native-plugins registry membership) is a capability-ORIGIN marker, not a trust boundary. What load time still enforces is NAME OWNERSHIP: a non-native plugin may not claim a reserved `provider_id` nor self-grant `official`. The `MOLECULE_DIGEST_PROVIDER_PLUGINS` env gate is removed from the workspace runtime. 0.6.0 — `contributes.state` declares that a plugin keeps DURABLE state across restarts (RFC molecule-ai-sdk#181, defect A of molecule-ai-workspace-runtime#360); the resolved per-plugin directory and its honest durability flag are delivered to daemons per plugin-state/plugin-state.contract.json. 0.5.0 — an mcpServers contribution may declare a scalar `audience` (self|org) that generalizes the `privileged` boolean into a declared audience→credential mapping (self-schedule v1 foundation, RFC plugin-mcp-audience-contract); RuntimeId is an open bounded/path-safe slug and official support is separate; 0.3.1 made daemons contribution semantics first-class.
title: Marketplace Plugin Manifest Contract
description: SSOT JSON-Schema (draft 2020-12) for the Molecule marketplace plugin manifest — the publishable shape of a `plugin.yaml` artifact (molecule-ai-plugin-* repos), authored marketplace-side per RFC molecule-core#3285 (Tool-Contract SSOT & Codegen). DERIVED FROM THE REAL ARTIFACTS + their CI validator: molecule-ai-plugin-molecule-careful-bash/plugin.yaml, image-gen/plugin.yaml, gh-identity/plugin.yaml, molecule-hitl/plugin.yaml, validated by each plugin repo's `.molecule-ci/scripts/validate-plugin.py` (required: name/version/description; runtimes must be a list; content is one of SKILL.md/hooks/skills/rules). The design is VS-Code-shaped: `engines` pins the minimum host version (like engines.vscode), and `contributes` is the OPEN, forward-compatible contribution surface — its KNOWN keys are validated by shape while UNKNOWN contribution points are tolerated. RuntimeId is an open bounded/path-safe slug; official first-party support is discovered separately from the adapter registry and never acts as a universal allowlist.

name.description: Plugin name (required by validate-plugin.py). The marketplace slug is derived from this. E.g. `molecule-careful-bash`, `image-gen`, `molecule-gh-identity`.

version.description: Plugin version (required). validate-plugin.py rejects any character outside `0-9.` — i.e. a dotted numeric version like `1.0.1` (no pre-release/build suffix). Modelled here with a numeric-dotted pattern mirroring that check.

publisher.description: Optional marketplace publisher/namespace (VS-Code `publisher`). Distinct from `author` (free-text attribution). Falls back to the org when absent.

author.description: Optional free-text author attribution as it appears in plugin.yaml (e.g. `Molecule AI`).

kind.description: Optional v1 plugin kind discriminator from plugin.yaml (e.g. `env-mutator` for the Go env-mutator class — gh-identity; `trigger` for a scheduler-style subprocess daemon — molecule-scheduler; `mcp-server` for an mcpServers-shaped plugin — molecule-platform; `digest-provider` for an in-process idle-digest DigestProvider — see `contributes.digestProviders`, RFC molecule-core#4413). Absent for skill/hook-class plugins. Open string (not enum) so new kinds are additive.

entrypoint.description: Optional Go entrypoint for code-class plugins (e.g. `pluginloader.BuildRegistry` — gh-identity). Absent for content-only plugins.

engines.description: Host-version constraints (VS-Code `engines`). Pins the minimum Molecule host the plugin requires.

runtimes.description: Runtime IDs this plugin supports. Items use the open RuntimeId contract; known aliases normalize separately.

skills.description: v0 shorthand: bare skill names contributed by the plugin (plugin.yaml `skills: [careful-mode]`). The richer structured form is `contributes.skills`.

hooks.description: v0 shorthand: bare hook names contributed by the plugin (plugin.yaml `hooks: [pre-bash-careful]`). The richer structured form is `contributes.hooks`.

rules.description: v0 shorthand: bare rule names contributed by the plugin. The richer structured form is `contributes.rules`.

contributes.description: VS-Code-shaped contribution surface. OPEN object: known contribution points are validated by shape; unknown ones are tolerated (forward-compat).

privileged.description: Whether the plugin requires org-admin / management privilege (e.g. the `molecule-platform` management MCP). image-gen explicitly documents `NOT privileged`. Absent/false = normal user capability.

sha256.description: Optional content digest of the published plugin artifact, for the marketplace integrity/attestation layer (Phase 3). Hex sha256.

runtimeId.description: Open, bounded, path-safe runtime identifier. Official first-party support is discovered separately; known aliases normalize without restricting third-party IDs.

engines.description: Host engine constraints, like VS-Code `engines`. `molecule` pins the minimum host version as a semver range. Open object so future host engines (e.g. a runtime-specific engine) are additive.

molecule.description: Minimum Molecule host version as a semver range, e.g. `^1.0`.

contributes.description: The contribution surface. KNOWN keys (skills/hooks/rules/mcpServers/commands v1; daemons per runtime#216; digestProviders per molecule-core#4413; state per RFC sdk#181) below are validated by shape. UNKNOWN keys (future contribution points such as `themes`, `tabs`, `canvasElements`) are explicitly TOLERATED via additionalProperties:true — adding a new contribution point MUST NOT fail validation against this schema (forward-compat). `daemons` itself landed exactly this way: the runtime shipped it as an additive point tolerated by this open object, and this schema now captures its shape descriptively.

hooks.description: Structured hook contributions (e.g. a PreToolUse:Bash hook).

mcpServers.description: MCP server contributions. An mcpServers-shaped plugin is resolved to the MCP server adaptor for any runtime (see mcp/mcp-plugin-delivery.contract.json). The entry shape mirrors the runtime-agnostic descriptor name->{command,args?,env?}.

daemons.description: Long-running daemon contributions (ADDITIVE contribution point, captured from reality per molecule-ai-workspace-runtime#216): the workspace runtime (molecule_runtime/plugin_daemons.py) spawns each declared daemon at boot, restarts it on crash with exponential backoff (circuit breaker after 10 consecutive fast failures), and kills it with the workspace — e.g. a channel bridge like lark-channel-molecule's `lark-bridge`. The entry shape deliberately mirrors `mcpServerContribution` (name + command/args?/env?) rather than inventing a new descriptor. VALIDATION SEMANTICS — deliberately UNCONSTRAINED here, mirroring the runtime exactly: the runtime NEVER rejects a manifest over `daemons`. A non-list value, non-mapping entries, missing/blank `name`/`command`, non-string `args` items, or a non-mapping `env` are SKIPPED with a loud warning at daemon discovery (`_entry_problem`) — never a boot crash, never a manifest-validation failure. Daemons are auxiliary; a typo here must not brick the plugin at the (future fail-closed) install gate, so schema-constraining this property would CHANGE runtime semantics rather than capture them (proven: runtime test test_malformed_entries_skipped_valid_kept fails against a strict version of this property). `$defs/daemonContribution` documents the canonical WELL-FORMED entry the runtime actually spawns — the shape emitters should produce and codegen consumers should use.

anyOf.description: The canonical, well-formed form — what emitters MUST produce. Kept as a live ref so the shape stays discoverable and $defs/daemonContribution is never orphaned.

Anything else — tolerated by design: the runtime skips non-conforming values/entries at spawn discovery with a warning instead of failing manifest validation. This branch makes the anyOf always-satisfiable, which IS the contract.

digestProviders.description: In-process idle-digest provider contributions (ADDITIVE contribution point, RFC molecule-core#4413 digest-providers-as-native-plugins). Each entry names a DigestProvider (idle-prompt/v1 contract) the workspace runtime imports IN-PROCESS and whose `contribute()` the idle-digest assembler awaits in the runtime event loop — unlike `daemons` (a spawned subprocess) or `mcpServers` (out-of-process config-file wiring), a digest provider is live Python loaded into the runtime. DELIVERY IS NOT NATIVE-ONLY: any plugin -- first-party or a customer's own -- may contribute a digest provider, and the workspace runtime imports and loads every declared provider BY DEFAULT, with no env gate and no operator opt-in. The platform is provider-agnostic: `native` (native-plugins registry membership) records that the PLATFORM ships that capability built-in, i.e. it is a capability-ORIGIN marker, not a trust boundary. In-process third-party execution was never gated elsewhere in the runtime either (`daemons` spawns manifest-declared subprocesses and the runtime plugins registry imports adaptor modules in-process, both flagless), so a native-only rule here bought no isolation while blocking every customer-shipped provider. ISOLATION, NOT ADMISSION CONTROL, is the mechanism: a provider that fails to import, construct or contribute is skipped/quarantined on its own and never costs anyone else the digest. VALIDATION SEMANTICS — deliberately UNCONSTRAINED here, mirroring the runtime and the idle-prompt failurePolicy: a malformed entry (or a non-list value) is SKIPPED with a warning at provider discovery (skip-and-degrade), never a manifest-validation failure, so a typo cannot brick the plugin at the (future fail-closed) install gate — schema-constraining this property would CHANGE runtime semantics rather than capture them, exactly as for `daemons`. TRUST (NAME OWNERSHIP — the one thing native status still decides) — `official` and the reserved band/id are NOT taken from the manifest at face value: the idle-prompt assembler derives them (reserved_provider_ids + pinned_reserved_to=identity-capabilities; urgency_grant=operator-approved-manifest), and its check_reserved_id DISABLES a third-party provider that claims a reserved provider_id. The workspace runtime enforces the same rule earlier and on the LOADED class rather than on the manifest: a provider from a non-native plugin whose loaded provider_id is reserved, or which self-declares official:true, is refused -- a reserved id names a PLATFORM-owned digest section, and `official` is the sole self-declared input to check_reserved_id, so a forged marker is precisely a forged licence to take a reserved id. The refusal is PER-PROVIDER: that one contribution is dropped and the plugin's other digestProviders still load. `$defs/digestProviderContribution` documents the canonical WELL-FORMED entry emitters should produce and codegen consumers should use.

anyOf.description: The canonical, well-formed form — what emitters MUST produce. Kept as a live ref so the shape stays discoverable and $defs/digestProviderContribution is never orphaned.

Anything else — tolerated by design: the runtime skips non-conforming values/entries at provider discovery with a warning instead of failing manifest validation. This branch makes the anyOf always-satisfiable, which IS the contract.

examples.summary: Open workspaces and pending provisions across the org.

configuration.description: Per-install configuration declaration (ADDITIVE contribution point). Declares WHICH keys an install may set and how to render them; the VALUES are delivered out-of-band as `/configs/plugin-settings/<install-name>.json` (from a workspace template's `plugins[].config`, org defaults, or an operator edit) and resolved by the workspace runtime at daemon discovery, where `${config:<key>}` references in a daemon's `env` are interpolated. VALIDATION SEMANTICS — deliberately UNCONSTRAINED here, mirroring `daemons` and `digestProviders`: the runtime DROPS bad keys and KEEPS the plugin (molecule_runtime/plugin_settings.load_delivered degrades to `{}` on malformed/oversize/missing settings and interpolate() renders an unresolvable reference as empty, never the literal), so a typo cannot brick the plugin at the (future fail-closed) install gate — schema-constraining this property would CHANGE runtime semantics rather than capture them. The declaration is descriptive only: the VALUE SPACE is free-form per plugin, so each trigger plugin defines its own config and nothing here constrains what a template may set. `$defs/configurationContribution` documents the canonical WELL-FORMED shape emitters, the `.example` generator, and the platform plugin tab should use.

anyOf.description: The canonical, well-formed form — what emitters MUST produce. Kept as a live ref so the shape stays discoverable and $defs/configurationContribution is never orphaned.
Anything else — tolerated by design: the runtime falls back to declared defaults instead of failing manifest validation. This branch makes the anyOf always-satisfiable, which IS the contract.

timezone.description: IANA timezone the cron grid is evaluated in.

state.description: DURABLE per-plugin state declaration (ADDITIVE contribution point, RFC molecule-ai-sdk#181 — defect A of molecule-ai-workspace-runtime#360). A plugin that must remember something ACROSS a container swap / instance recreate — a channel plugin's poll cursor is the motivating case — declares that here instead of GUESSING a path. Before this key there was NO word in the manifest for durable state, so `gmail-channel-molecule` guessed `~/.gmail-channel` (ephemeral root layer), then `/workspace/.gmail-channel` (MEASURED also wiped on local-docker, whose restart path destroys and re-seeds the `/workspace` volume), and its Gmail cursor re-pinned to `now()` on every restart — silently swallowing every older message. Four daemon plugins reached four incompatible answers to the same question (`/workspace`, `Path.home()`, `CONFIGS_DIR`, and a `MOLECULE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR` that nothing set), which is what makes this a contract gap rather than four independent bugs. NOT A NEW MECHANISM: the runtime already resolves and injects a per-plugin-class state dir for `kind: trigger` daemons (`molecule_runtime/trigger_state.py`, `MOLECULE_TRIGGER_STATE_DIR`); this key is that seam made kind-agnostic, plugin-keyed and durable-rooted. PRESENCE is the declaration; the block carries only how loudly to complain when the substrate cannot honour it. DELIVERY is NOT described here — it is the plugin-state contract (plugin-state/plugin-state.contract.json), which owns the reserved daemon env vars (`MOLECULE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR` + `MOLECULE_PLUGIN_STATE_DURABLE`), the per-plugin directory template, the provisioner-declared durability signal, and the degradation policy. ISOLATION — the directory is keyed on the VALIDATED MANIFEST NAME, never on a plugin-supplied path: a manifest cannot name, redirect, or escape its own state dir, and the env vars are RESERVED (stripped from the inherited environment before a daemon's own `env` map is applied, exactly like the channel A2A socket vars), so a manifest `env:` block cannot forge them. All of a plugin's daemons share ONE directory — they are one plugin and one trust domain. VALIDATION SEMANTICS — deliberately UNCONSTRAINED here, mirroring `daemons`, `digestProviders` and `configuration`: a malformed `state` value is treated as a bare declaration (durability defaults to `required`) and logged, never a manifest-validation failure, so a typo cannot brick the plugin at the (future fail-closed) install gate. `$defs/stateContribution` documents the canonical WELL-FORMED shape emitters should produce and codegen consumers should use.

anyOf.description: The canonical, well-formed form — what emitters MUST produce. Kept as a live ref so the shape stays discoverable and $defs/stateContribution is never orphaned.

Anything else — tolerated by design: the runtime treats an unreadable declaration as a bare `durability: required` and warns, instead of failing manifest validation. This branch makes the anyOf always-satisfiable, which IS the contract.

examples.description: Gmail poll cursor — the high-water mark of already-relayed mail. Losing it re-pins the mark to now() and every older message becomes permanently invisible.

stateContribution.description: The canonical well-formed shape of `contributes.state` — a plugin's declaration that it keeps state which MUST survive a container swap / instance recreate. There are no path, name, size or quota fields BY DESIGN: the platform, not the plugin, chooses where the directory lives (that is the whole defect being fixed), and a per-plugin quota is a separate concern with no consumer today. The only authored field is `durability`, which selects the degradation posture — the one thing the platform genuinely cannot infer.

durability.description: How the plugin degrades when the substrate has NO durable storage (no provisioner-supplied state root — e.g. an EC2 workspace with the per-org data volume off, or any substrate the provisioner has not wired). The runtime ALWAYS injects a writable directory and ALWAYS reports the truth in `MOLECULE_PLUGIN_STATE_DURABLE`; this field selects only how loudly the platform complains and how the plugin is expected to behave. `required` (the default, and the correct value for anything holding a cursor / high-water mark): losing the state causes SILENT DATA LOSS, so the runtime logs at WARNING naming the plugin, and the plugin is expected to visibly degrade — e.g. use a bounded lookback plus id-dedup rather than pinning a cursor to now(). `preferred`: the state is a cache or an optimization, losing it costs work but not correctness, so the runtime logs at INFO and the plugin may silently start cold. NEITHER value ever refuses to spawn the daemon: a channel bridge that runs lossily still delivers today's mail, whereas one the platform refuses to start delivers nothing — and the runtime's daemon posture is already `failures are logged, never fatal`.

description.description: Optional human-readable statement of WHAT is kept and what breaks if it is lost. Surfaced by the platform plugin tab and by the runtime's degradation warning, so an operator reading a `state is not durable on this substrate` warning learns the consequence, not just the fact.

path.description: Optional path to the skill content within the plugin.

event.description: Optional host event the hook binds to (e.g. `PreToolUse:Bash`).

mcpServerContribution.description: A single contributed MCP server descriptor (runtime-agnostic name->{command,args?,env?}).

env.description: Optional environment map (var->value) for the MCP server process.

privileged.description: Whether this MCP server is the privileged management surface.

audience.description: Declared AUDIENCE of this MCP surface — WHO the runtime injects a credential for (RFC plugin-mcp-audience-contract, self-schedule v1). PER-SERVER: a plugin that exposes both audiences declares TWO mcpServers entries, one per audience. `self` = the workspace acting as ITSELF — the runtime injects the workspace token as a re-read FILE PATH (MOLECULE_WORKSPACE_TOKEN_FILE=/configs/.auth_token; the mcp-server re-reads the restart-rotated file per call — injecting the MOLECULE_WORKSPACE_TOKEN env VALUE instead would 401 after rotation), scoped to its own workspace :id (a foreign id fails closed); the self-schedule tool is the first consumer. `org` = the org/platform agent — the runtime injects the org API key (MOLECULE_ORG_API_KEY, tenant-admin), ANCHORED to a core-verified management/platform MCP name (MANAGEMENT_MCP_NAME) — never an ordinary or self-declared workspace plugin (core's platform_agent invariant). This field is the successor to `privileged` (`privileged:true` corresponds to `audience:"org"`). When `audience` is ABSENT, the runtime injects the org credential ONLY for the name-anchored management/platform MCP (MANAGEMENT_MCP_NAME) and injects NOTHING otherwise — a self-declared `audience:"org"` on an ordinary tenant plugin obtains NO org creds — preserving existing behavior with no flag-day. See mcp/mcp-plugin-delivery.contract.json#/audiences for the audience -> {mcp_mode, credential_env} delivery mapping the runtime honors. v1 wires ONLY `self`; `org` is declared in the contract but its credential injection is deferred (kept anchored to a core-verified kind=platform signal, not a self-declared field).

daemonContribution.description: A single contributed long-running daemon, exactly the shape molecule-ai-workspace-runtime's plugin_daemons.py parses (runtime#216): `{name, command, args?, env?, cwd?}`. The runtime spawns `[command, *args]` in its own session/process group, with the workspace process env overlaid with `env`, in `cwd` (plugin-dir-relative; default: the plugin dir itself). Requiredness and item types mirror the runtime's `_entry_problem` checks verbatim: non-mapping entry, missing/whitespace-only `name` or `command`, non-string-list `args`, and non-mapping `env` are what the runtime SKIPS (with a warning) — everything else it accepts. First real consumer: lark-channel-molecule's `plugin.yaml` (`{name: lark-bridge, command: bash, args: [daemon-bootstrap.sh]}`).

name.description: Daemon name (required, non-blank — the runtime rejects a missing/empty/whitespace-only name). Namespaced by the owning plugin into the supervisor key `<plugin>/<name>`, so two plugins may both declare a daemon called `bridge`.

command.description: Launch command (required, non-blank), e.g. `bash` or `python`. The spawned argv is `[command, *args]`.

args.description: Optional command arguments. Must be a list of strings — the runtime skips the entry on any non-string item.

env.description: Optional environment map (var→value) overlaid on the workspace process env for the daemon. The runtime rejects only a non-mapping `env`; it str()-coerces non-string VALUES rather than rejecting them — string values are the canonical form. An explicitly-null `env` is treated as absent by the runtime (YAML `env:` with no value), though this schema's canonical form is to omit the key.

cwd.description: Optional working directory, resolved against the plugin dir when relative (default: the plugin dir itself). The runtime never validates `cwd` — a non-string value is str()-coerced rather than rejected; a string path is the canonical form.

digestProviderContribution.description: A single contributed in-process idle-digest provider (idle-prompt/v1 DigestProvider). The workspace runtime imports `entrypoint` as a DigestProvider and the idle-digest assembler awaits its `contribute()` each idle tick, applying the idle-prompt trust/failure policy. First real consumers: the platform digest legos being extracted from the runtime's hardcoded roster (goal-state, task-queue, identity-capabilities, sent-folder, inbound-a2a) into native plugins per RFC molecule-core#4413.

provider_id.description: The digest provider id the idle-prompt assembler keys trust + render tier on (idle-prompt providerDecl.provider_id), and which MUST equal the loaded DigestProvider's `provider_id`. Reserved official ids (identity-capabilities, task-queue, sent-folder, inbound-a2a, delegation-results, scheduler, goal-state) name PLATFORM-owned digest sections and survive the assembler's check_reserved_id ONLY when the loaded class is official=True AND delivered through the native-plugins registry; a third-party plugin claiming a reserved id has that ONE contribution refused at load and is never rendered, while its sibling contributions still load. This is the only respect in which native status matters -- it governs which NAMES a plugin may claim, never whether the plugin's code may run.

entrypoint.description: In-process import target the runtime loads as a DigestProvider, `module:ClassName` (e.g. `molecule_digest_goal.provider:GoalStateProvider`), resolved against the installed plugin dir. IN-PROCESS load (contribute() awaited in the runtime idle loop) is what distinguishes a digest provider from a subprocess `daemon` or an out-of-process `mcpServer`. It does NOT restrict delivery to native plugins: the runtime imports the entrypoint of every declared provider, whatever the plugin's origin.

base_tier.description: Optional REQUESTED base render rank (idle-prompt providerDecl.base_tier; lower renders earlier within the base band). Advisory only: the assembler applies the idle-prompt trustPolicy — a third-party provider is placed at third_party_default_tier and cannot self-grant band=pinned or urgency (urgency_grant=operator-approved-manifest).

summary.description: Optional human-readable one-line summary of the section this provider renders (idle-prompt providerDecl.summary).

description.description: Optional human-readable description of the contribution.

configurationContribution.description: The canonical well-formed shape of `contributes.configuration`. PROPERTY NAMES must match the workspace runtime's reference grammar (`^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$` — molecule_runtime/plugin_settings._CONFIG_REF): a key outside it can be declared but could never be referenced as `${config:<key>}`, so the canonical branch rejects it while the tolerant branch of the property still accepts the manifest.

title.description: Section heading for the platform plugin tab.

properties.description: Declared key -> declaration. Each key is referenced from a daemon's env as `${config:<key>}`.

configurationProperty.description: One declared, per-install configurable key — the unit the three consumers share. An ECOSYSTEM DEVELOPER reads `default` to run the plugin with no API call; an OPERATOR reads `description`/`enum` to review and reuse a value across workspaces; the PLATFORM UI renders the plugin tab from `type`/`enum`/`default` and masks the field when `sensitive`.

type.description: JSON type used to render and coerce the field.

default.description: Layer-1 value. Lives in the manifest ON THE BOX — core cannot supply it at provision time (it holds no manifest then), so the runtime resolves it at daemon-discovery time.

description.description: Human-facing help, shown in the plugin tab and emitted into the generated `.example`.

items.description: One allowed value, of whatever JSON type `type` declares.

enum.description: Closed value set; the UI renders a select rather than a free text field.

sensitive.description: True for credential-shaped values. The UI masks the field and the generated `.example` carries a PLACEHOLDER, never a real value; non-sensitive keys may carry a real example value.

required.description: Advisory only. An unset required key resolves to empty like any other unresolved reference — it does NOT fail the install, because the runtime drops bad keys and keeps the plugin.
